app_fee.value: The application fee for international applicants is USD 105 per application (USD 95 for domestic).
app_fee.quote: As of August 1, 2023, the fee for international applicants is $105 per application.

fee_waiver.value: Institute-level waivers only cover listed programs (e.g., Fulbright, McNair, GEM, recruiting events); Georgia Tech does not grant hardship waivers to international applicants, though some departments may consider their own waiver. Internationals must submit all materials, including English scores, before requesting one.
fee_waiver.quote: The Office of Graduate Education provides Institute-level application fee waivers for participants of the specific programs listed below. | The Office of Graduate Education does not review or approve requests based on financial hardship for international applicants. | If you don't meet the criteria for an Institute-level waiver, we encourage you to reach out directly to the graduate program you are applying to.

also.quote: International applicants must submit all required application materials prior to requesting a fee waiver.

gre_general.value: Georgia Tech sets no Institute-wide GRE rule; each program decides (see the program records).

toefl_min.value: TOEFL iBT 90 overall with 19+ in each section (tests before January 2026), or 4.5 on the new scale (Reading/Listening/Writing 4+, Speaking 3.5+). Many programs require more; MyBest scores and Duolingo/PTE are not accepted.
toefl_min.quote: TOEFL iBT Prior to January 2026: 90 or higher TOEFL iBT After January 2026: 4.5 or higher | Below are minimum institutional requirements. Individual graduate programs may require higher scores.

ielts_min.value: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with Reading, Listening and Speaking 6.5+ and Writing 5.5+.
ielts_min.quote: IELTS Academic 7 or higher Reading ≥ 6.5 Listening ≥ 6.5 Speaking ≥ 6.5 Writing ≥ 5.5

english_waiver.value: From Fall 2027, India is not on the approved-country list, but a post-secondary degree taught in English satisfies the requirement if confirmed by a transcript notation, institutional letter or Medium of Instruction certificate; otherwise a TOEFL/IELTS score is needed.
english_waiver.quote: Applicant has earned a post-secondary degree and can confirm English was the official language of instruction through one of these documents: Transcript notation Institutional letter Medium of Instruction certificate | If English was the language of instruction for your degree program, you may satisfy the English proficiency requirement by providing documentation from your institution confirming this.

also.quote: You have earned a post-secondary degree in one of the countries listed below.

notes: New for Fall 2027: citizenship alone no longer satisfies the English requirement; an English-medium degree (with MOI proof) does. TOEFL MyBest, Duolingo and PTE are not accepted. Several departments set higher English minimums.
